builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
summary: It replaces surrogate drafter training objectives (cross-entropy, KL, total variation, and block-level approximations such as WTV, VSD, DBLast) with an unbiased estimate of expected acceptance length using path weights and Rao-Blackwellization, requiring only a change to the training loss and no change to drafter architecture or inference. The cost is retraining the drafter with a more complex loss, plus the implementation and validation effort of integrating the reference code; inference-time memory and latency are unchanged. It can fail if acceptance-length gains measured under probabilistic serving do not transfer to the reader's target model, drafter, sampling settings, or task mix, and unbiasedness does not guarantee superiority over tuned baselines in every workload.
rationale: The method is a drop-in training-loss change compatible with a single GPU for drafter training and directly targets the quantity that determines speculative decoding speedup, but the reported gains are demonstrated on one target-drafter pair, so adoption should follow a workload-specific acceptance-length benchmark against the reader's current baseline.
technique: REAL loss for speculative drafter training

claims.statement: It replaces surrogate drafter training objectives (cross-entropy, KL, total variation, and block-level approximations such as WTV, VSD, DBLast) with an unbiased estimate of expected acceptance length using path weights and Rao-Blackwellization, requiring only a change to the training loss and no change to drafter architecture or inference. The cost is retraining the drafter with a more complex loss, plus the implementation and validation effort of integrating the reference code; inference-time memory and latency are unchanged. It can fail if acceptance-length gains measured under probabilistic serving do not transfer to the reader's target model, drafter, sampling settings, or task mix, and unbiasedness does not guarantee superiority over tuned baselines in every workload.

REAL outperforms WTV, VSD, DBLast, and a static LK baseline on probabilistic serving acceptance length across 9 task subsets and 5 evaluation seeds with a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B target and Domino drafter; no speedup factor is reported.
